correctness.rationale: The conditional PD increment is a sum of edge indicators; the shared independent extinction probability yields the exact clade-size polynomial. At a two-taxon LCA shared path terms cancel and ultrametricity forces a factor (q-1). Every LCA split with <=6 descendant taxa has a fixed-sign, linear, or strictly monotone residual, proving <=1 strict interior reversal. At seven taxa splits (1,6),(2,5),(3,4) admit at most two. Twelve explicit rational edges yield binary positive-length height-four phylogeny and HED difference (q-1)(q-3/10)(q-4/5), giving exactly two simple strict crossings. An added binary root preserves the difference for arbitrarily many taxa. Re-running the standalone checker validated the edge counts, descendant sizes, seven heights, both HED polynomials, and 3136 exact survivor-state summands; finite checks do not replace the universal proof.

value.rationale: HED is an established conservation-ranking input sensitive to the extinction probabilities of other taxa. Two strict priority flips for one pair on a single fixed ultrametric phylogeny show that no universal monotone, single-threshold comparative response to a homogeneous extinction scenario is available. Seven taxa is the exact first feasible size; the 4-versus-3 clade split explains the quadratic mechanism and supports a meaningful natural small-object boundary, rather than an arbitrary numerical sample. The result is a structural stress test and makes no unsupported claim of empirical frequency or optimal management policy.
